1.1. Petitioner states that the Company was originally incorporated as a private limited company on 21.02.1985 and was converted into a public limited company in 1992.

The Company is engaged in the manufacture of pharmaceutical products in the areas of peptides, advanced organic chemistry,
chiral chemistry and biotechnology.
The Company has two subsidiaries, namely Vix Sven Genetech Ltd and Jupiter Bioscience Inc., USA, both operating outside India.

It also engaged in manufacture of peptide raw materials, intermediates and finished active pharmaceutical ingredients (A.P.L.),
polyester yarn, organic drug intermediates and A.P.I., and specialty and fine chemicals.

From a perusal of the material on record, it is to be noted that Company availed two term loans and one corporate loan aggregating to Rs.56 crores during 2008 and 2009.

The loan account was classified as Non-Performing Asset on 31.03.2011 with total dues aggregating to Rs.47.37 crores,
excluding applicable interest and charges.

The amount involved in the fraud is stated to be Rs.47.37 crores, which is far in excess of the threshold prescribed under the RBI Master Directions.

read with Master Direction No.RBI/2024-25/118 dated 15.07.2024.

sentences.text: The statutory character of directions issued under Section 35A is well recognized.
Consequently, once a fraud exceeding Rs.6 crores is detected and classified, a reporting bank is under a binding obligation to report the matter to CBI in the prescribed format.

In compliance with the said mandate, Petitioner submitted complaint dated 29.04.2024 to Respondent No.3, which admitted that complaint was received and assigned No.RA03520240017 and that discrepancies were communicated by letter dated 31.07.2024.

A revised complaint dated 28.11.2024 was also received and assigned No.RA0352024A0023 and further discrepancies were intimated by letter dated 16.12.2024.
8.

The principal ground on which Respondent No.3 declined to register a case is withdrawal of general consent under Section 6 of the Delhi Special Police Establishment Act, 1946 by the Government of Telangana vide G.O.Ms.No.51 dated 30.08.2022.
Section 6 stipulates that members of the Delhi Special Police Establishment shall not exercise powers and jurisdiction in a State without the consent of the Government of that State.

Upon withdrawal of general consent,
case-specific consent is required.

9. Respondent No.1, in its counter affidavit, has unequivocally stated that if CBI forwards a proposal seeking specific consent in respect of the subject complaint, the Government of Telangana would consider the same on merits and, upon being satisfied with the necessity of investigation, accord permission under Section 6 of the DSPE Act.
Thus, the statutory mechanism for obtaining consent is neither closed nor unavailable; it merely requires initiation by the investigating agency.
The stand of Respondent No.3 is that before approaching the State Government for specific consent, the complaint must be free from discrepancies.

This Court is unable to accept that such discrepancies,
even if assumed to exist, can operate as a jurisdictional embargo against registration of a case in respect of a fraud quantified at Rs.47.37 crores, supported by a forensic audit report dated 14.06.2023 and preceded by classification as fraud and reporting to RBI.

10. It is relevant to note that in respect of the same borrower, on the complaint of IFCI, CBI case RC0352022A0007 dated 28.03.2022 was registered and charge-sheet was filed on 29.11.2023 before the XXI Additional Chief Metropolitan Magistrate, Nampally, Hyderabad.

entities.text: XXI Additional Chief Metropolitan Magistrate, Nampally, Hyderabad
entities.label: COURT

sentences.text: This fact demonstrates that investigation by CBI into transactions of the said Company is neither unprecedented nor legally impermissible.

The scheme of the DSPE Act contemplates that the investigating agency, upon receipt of information disclosing commission of a cognizable offence,
proceeds in accordance with law and, where required, seeks consent from the State Government.

The reporting bank has no statutory competence to seek consent under Section 6 and obligation cast upon Petitioner flows from RBI directions; the power and responsibility to seek consent rests with the investigating agency.

11. If Respondent No.3, after receiving the complaint and assigning it a registration number for scrutiny, were to refrain from taking further steps solely on the ground of absence of general consent, without initiating the process for obtaining specific consent, the statutory reporting framework under the RBI Master Directions would be rendered nugatory.
Such an interpretation would create a legal vacuum whereby frauds of substantial magnitude escape investigation on account of procedural impasse.

sentences.text:
The discrepancies pointed out by Respondent No.3 pertain to internal investigation reports,
ABBFF advice, inconsistent figures and certain contradictory statements.
These are matters capable of clarification or investigation during the course of enquiry.
They do not negate the existence of an allegation of fraud involving Rs.47.37 crores.
Registration of a case is not an adjudication on merits but initiation of investigative process.
The threshold for such initiation cannot be elevated to a standard that defeats statutory mandates.
Respondent No.3 itself asserts that it has not barred Petitioner from filing a fresh complaint and is ready to deal with the matter after removal of discrepancies.
Respondent No.1 has expressed willingness to consider a proposal for specific consent.
In such circumstances, continued inaction in not initiating steps to seek specific consent and proceed in accordance with law lacks reasonable justification.
13. Article 14 of the Constitution mandates that State action must be fair, non-arbitrary and in conformity with law.
Where a statutory authority is vested with power coupled with duty, such power must be exercised in furtherance of the statutory scheme.
Refusal to exercise jurisdiction on grounds not germane to the object of the statute would amount to arbitrariness.

This Court is therefore of the considered view that while Respondent No.3 was justified in pointing out discrepancies for purposes of completeness, it was not justified in treating the withdrawal of general consent as an absolute bar and in refraining from initiating the process for obtaining case- specific consent from the State Government in a matter involving alleged fraud of Rs. 47.37 crores.

The inaction of Respondent No.3 in taking steps to seek specific consent under Section 6 of the DSPE Act and to proceed in accordance with law, despite statutory reporting obligations arising under RBI Master Direction No.RBI/2024-25/118 dated 15.07.2024, is arbitrary and unsustainable in law.
14. Accordingly, the Writ Petition is allowed.

Respondent No.3 is directed to process the complaint dated 28.11.2024 of Petitioner and take appropriate steps, in accordance with Section 6 of the Delhi Special Police Establishment Act, 1946, to seek specific consent from Respondent No.1 for investigation of the allegations pertaining to M/s Jupiter Bio Sciences Limited involving fraud quantified at Rs.47.37 crores.
Upon receipt of such proposal, Respondent No.1 shall consider the same on its own merits, in accordance with law, and pass appropriate orders expeditiously.
In the event of grant of consent, Respondent No.3 shall proceed to register a case and conduct investigation strictly in accordance with law.
No costs.
15. Pending miscellaneous applications, if any, shall stand closed.

Such an interpretation would create a legal vacuum whereby frauds of substantial magnitude escape investigation on account of procedural impasse.
They do not negate the existence of an allegation of fraud involving Rs.47.37 crores.
Registration of a case is not an adjudication on merits but initiation of investigative process.
The threshold for such initiation cannot be elevated to a standard that defeats statutory mandates.
Respondent No.3 itself asserts that it has not barred Petitioner from filing a fresh complaint and is ready to deal with the matter after removal of discrepancies.
Respondent No.1 has expressed willingness to consider a proposal for specific consent.
In such circumstances, continued inaction in not initiating steps to seek specific consent and proceed in accordance with law lacks reasonable justification.
13. Article 14 of the Constitution mandates that State action must be fair, non-arbitrary and in conformity with law.
Where a statutory authority is vested with power coupled with duty, such power must be exercised in furtherance of the statutory scheme.
Refusal to exercise jurisdiction on grounds not germane to the object of the statute would amount to arbitrariness.
This Court is therefore of the considered view that while Respondent No.3 was justified in pointing out discrepancies for purposes of completeness, it was not justified in treating the withdrawal of general consent as an absolute bar and in refraining from initiating the process for obtaining case- specific consent from the State Government in a matter involving alleged fraud of Rs. 47.37 crores.
The inaction of Respondent No.3 in taking steps to seek specific consent under Section 6 of the DSPE Act and to proceed in accordance with law, despite statutory reporting obligations arising under RBI Master Direction No.RBI/2024-25/118 dated 15.07.2024, is arbitrary and unsustainable in law.
opennyai_summary.decision:
14. Accordingly, the Writ Petition is allowed.
Respondent No.3 is directed to process the complaint dated 28.11.2024 of Petitioner and take appropriate steps, in accordance with Section 6 of the Delhi Special Police Establishment Act, 1946, to seek specific consent from Respondent No.1 for investigation of the allegations pertaining to M/s Jupiter Bio Sciences Limited involving fraud quantified at Rs.47.37 crores.
Upon receipt of such proposal, Respondent No.1 shall consider the same on its own merits, in accordance with law, and pass appropriate orders expeditiously.
In the event of grant of consent, Respondent No.3 shall proceed to register a case and conduct investigation strictly in accordance with law.
No costs.
15. Pending miscellaneous applications, if any, shall stand closed.
